subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, trust, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This would define a public plugin/security boundary around persisted config, auth, provider, and SecretRef-adjacent writes, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent SDK contract or fail-open/fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Design the API first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

options.title: Rely on built-in guards
options.body: Decline the plugin veto and rescope this issue around the existing schema validation, SecretRef preflight, baseHash checks, destructive-array guard, and agent-tool allowlist.

options.title: Limit to agent tool writes
options.body: Add a narrower guard for model-initiated `gateway` config writes while accepting that other writers remain outside a plugin veto path.

recommendation.title: Design the API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle hook ordering and metadata in the config validation/mutation direction, then implement the agreed SDK contract with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They already provided the strongest product-routing review tying this item to config validation/mutation design.
